articles.title: Notícias g1 Triângulo: Corpo em imóvel e febre amarela em Patos | G1
articles.standfirst: Resumo de notícias da semana entre os dias 7 e 13 de novembro.
articles.summary: O g1 Triângulo destaca o corpo achado em imóvel de leilão, o alerta de febre amarela em Patos de Minas e a demissão de servidora com 239 faltas em Uberlândia.
articles.body:
Confira o que foi destaque no g1 Triângulo nesta semana, com as notícias mais acessadas entre os dias 7 e 13 de novembro.

marilene de fátima mulher encontrada morta apartamento patos de minas leilão — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Uma mulher encontrou um corpo em avançado estado de decomposição no quarto de um apartamento após comprar o imóvel em um leilão em Patos de Minas . O corpo foi identificado como o de Marilene de Fátima, de 53 anos, antiga proprietária do imóvel, que estaria morta há mais de um ano.

A compradora, Kalina Poliana, contou que recebeu permissão do filho da antiga proprietária para entrar no apartamento após a compra. Com a ajuda de um chaveiro, ela conseguiu entrar no local e encontrou o corpo envolto em uma coberta em cima de uma cama.

"Foi muito complicado, eu fiquei muito abalada. Eu já tinha falado com o filho da proprietária, ele me falou que ela tinha sumido, tinha arrumado um suposto namorado. Ela comentou que iria morar com o rapaz em Varjão de Minas", afirmou ela.

Segundo o irmão de Marilene, que não quis se identificar, afirmou que a família perdeu o contato com ela em outubro de 2025 . Na época, ela ligou dizendo que o apartamento havia sido penhorado e pediu R$ 1,8 mil emprestados. Ele respondeu que não tinha o dinheiro.

A suspeita é que ela estivesse morta há aproximadamente um ano.

"É triste que isso tenha acontecido. Agora, vamos descobrir o que aconteceu. Infelizmente, não conseguimos perceber a tempo. Agora é seguir em frente", lamentou.

A Prefeitura de Patos de Minas confirmou que um macaco encontrado morto próximo à comunidade de Moreiras, na zona rural do município, testou positivo para febre amarela em outubro. Desde então, agentes comunitários de saúde visitaram moradores para conferir os cartões de vacinação, enquanto equipes da Vigilância de Zoonoses fazem buscas por outros primatas mortos na região.

Em nota, a prefeitura reforçou que os macacos não transmitem a febre amarela, mas são importantes “sentinelas”, pois indicam que o vírus está em circulação no local. A transmissão ocorre pela picada de mosquitos infectados, e a vacinação é a principal medida de prevenção.

O exame realizado no animal recolhido confirmou a presença do vírus, mas não especificou a sublinhagem identificada.

A orientação da prefeitura é que, caso a população encontre primatas doentes ou mortos, não toque nos animais nem tente removê-los. A ocorrência deve ser comunicada ao Centro de Controle de Zoonoses, pelo telefone (34) 3822-9624, das 7h às 18h, por ligação ou WhatsApp. É importante informar a localização do animal.

Uma servidora da rede municipal de ensino de Uberlândia foi demitida após apresentar atestados médicos falsos, acumular 239 faltas injustificadas (quase oito meses) e se mudar para outro país mesmo com o pedido de licença negado pela Prefeitura.

A decisão, publicada no Diário Oficial do Município (DOM) na quarta-feira (11), ainda determina o ressarcimento aos cofres públicos dos valores recebidos durante os períodos de licença considerados indevidos. O valor não foi informado.

Segundo o Município, durante o processo administrativo que investigava a idoneidade dos atestados apresentados, o hospital informou a inexistência de prontuários, atendimentos ou emissões de documentos em nome da servidora nas datas que constavam nos documentos apresentados à Prefeitura.

A apuração da Prefeitura também apontou que a servidora deixou de comparecer ao trabalho entre agosto de 2025 e março de 2026. Conforme a decisão, ela manteve os planos de mudança para o exterior mesmo após o pedido de licença ter sido indeferido.

articles.title: Trump rules out cyberattack, AI as US probes nationwide flight disruption
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the nationwide flight disruption was unlikely to have been caused by a cyberattack or artificial
articles.body: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that the nationwide flight disruption was unlikely to have been caused by a cyberattack or artificial intelligence, as authorities continued to investigate the telecommunications outage that prompted the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a ground stop across the country.US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said there was no indication that a national security threat was behind the disruption, seeking to distinguish the incident from the September 11, 2001, attacks."This isn’t the same comparison to 9/11," Mullin told reporters outside the White House, assuring them that all flights had been accounted for and passengers were safe.Also Read| US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so farMullin said authorities had no reason to believe the communications failure was linked to a threat against the United States, although he did not rule out any possible cause, including a cyberattack."There is no indication that we’ve had, no reason to believe, that as of right now this was a threat to the United States," he said, adding that there was "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack against us.""This was a telecommunication outage," Mullin said.The Homeland Security Secretary confirmed that Trump had been briefed on the FAA's nationwide ground stop and had spoken with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. He said the President had taken an active role in coordinating the response and ensuring that officials had the necessary resources."He was on the phone earlier with the president and several of us. And they’re doing a phenomenal job in a crisis mode," Mullin said, referring to the coordination among officials.He added that Trump "took a lead in this immediately" to ensure the situation was managed.Mullin also dismissed any connection between the FAA telecommunications outage and a major Microsoft outage reported a day earlier."I don’t see any reason to connect those two at all," he said, adding, "Those are separate issues."The FAA had earlier ordered a nationwide ground stop after a temporary telecommunications outage affected all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, disrupting flight operations across the country.Also Read| US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US operationsDuffy announced the disruption in a post on X, saying FAA technicians were investigating the communications failure."The @FAAnews issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them," Duffy said.The FAA said the suspension was a precautionary measure and that international arrivals would be handled on a case-by-case basis."There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis," the agency said in a post on X.According to flight-tracking platform FlightAware, around 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled following the ground stop. The disruption affected all 22 regional air traffic control centres, which are responsible for guiding aircraft within their respective regions.Data from Flightradar24 showed that around 4,042 flights were airborne and heading towards US airports when the ground stop was issued.The precise cause of the telecommunications outage remained unclear. An airline source told CNN that the FAA was still investigating the disruption and had yet to establish what had happened."The FAA doesn't know yet what is going on; it is affecting different facilities in different ways," the source told CNN, adding that a crisis call had been held without a clear explanation for the outage.Mullin said authorities were continuing to assess the situation, reiterating that all flights had been accounted for and passengers were safe.You use AI every day. articles.title: Happy Children's Day 2026: 25+ Inspirational quotes by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru to inspire students
articles.summary: Every year, 14 November is celebrated as Children’s Day in India. It is one of those days that even adults remember cherishing.
articles.body: Every year, 14 November is celebrated as Children’s Day in India. It is one of those days that even adults remember cherishing. When asked about their school days, they often end up explaining how their classes ended early, teachers smiled a little more, and someone handed out sweets.Every year, children look forward to expressing the joy of that feeling. Some want a poem, some want a joke, and many a times, people often tend to some inspiratikonal quotes especially from Chacha Nehru who loved and adored children.This year, the day marks Jawaharlal Nehru's 137th birth anniversary, who was born on 14 November 1889 in Prayagraj.Why is 14 November celebrated as Children’s Day every year?Interestingly, the date has not always been the same. Children's Day was celebrated on 20 November before Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru's death, matching the UN's Universal Children's Day. But after he died on 27 May 1964, Parliament passed a resolution making his birth anniversary the official date. So the day honours both children and the man who was known for his affection for them.Here are some inspirational quotes by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru to remember on Children’s Day, according to Goodreads.“We live in a wonderful world that is full of beauty, charm and adventure. There is no end to the adventures we can have if only we seek them with our eyes open.”“Facts are facts and will not disappear on account of your likes.”“A language is something infinitely greater than grammar and philology. It is the poetic testament of the genius of a race and a culture, and the living embodiment of the thoughts and fancies that have moulded them”“There is nothing more horrifying than stupidity in action.”“Life is like a game of cards. The hand that is dealt you is determinism; the way you play it is free will.”“The policy of being too cautious is the greatest risk of all.”“Evil unchecked grows, evil tolerated poisons the whole system.”“It is science alone that can solve the problems of hunger and poverty, of insanitation and illiteracy, of superstition and deadening custom and tradition, of vast resources running to waste, or a rich country inhabited by starving people... Who indeed could afford to ignore science today? At every turn we have to seek its aid... The future belongs to science and those who make friends with science.”“India has known the innocence and insouciance of childhood, the passion and abandon of youth, and the ripe wisdom of maturity that comes from long experience of pain and pleasure; and over and over a gain she has renewed her childhood and youth and age”“Culture is the widening of the mind and of the spirit.”“The forces in a capitalist society, if left unchecked, tend to make the rich richer and the poor poorer.”“What the mysterious is I do not know. I do not call it God because God has come to mean much that I do not believe in. I find myself incapable of thinking of a deity or of any unknown supreme power in anthropomorphic terms, and the fact that many people think so is continually a source of surprise to me. Any idea of a personal God seems very odd to me.”“Without that passion and urge, there is a gradual oozing out of hope and vitality, a settling down on lower levels of existence, a slow merging into non-existence. We become prisoners of the past and some part of its immobility sticks to us.”“Politics and Religion are obsolete. The time has come for Science and Spirituality.”“Long years ago, we made a tryst with destiny, and now the time comes when we shall redeem our pledge, not wholly or in full measure, but very substantially. At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom. A moment comes, which comes but rarely in history, when we step out from the old to the new, when an age ends, and when the soul of a nation, long suppressed, finds utterance”“The spectacle of what is called religion, or at any rate organised religion, in India and elsewhere, has filled me with horror and I have frequently condemned it and wished to make a clean sweep of it. Almost always it seemed to stand for blind belief and reaction, dogma and bigotry, superstition, exploitation and the preservation of vested interests.”“The best and noblest gifts of humanity cannot be the monopoly of a particular race or country; its scope may not be limited nor may it be regarded as the miser's hoard buried underground.”“If any person raises his hand to strike down another on the ground of religion, I shall fight him till the last breath of my life, both as the head of the government and from the outside”“The ideals and objectives of yesterday was still ideals of today, but they lost some of their luster and even, as one seemed to go towards them, they lost the shining beauty which had warmed the heart and vitalized the body. Evil triumphed often enough, but what was far worse was the coarsening and distortion of what seemed so right. Was human nature so essentially bad that it would take ages of training ,through suffering and misfortune, before it could behave reasonably and raise man above the creature of lust and violence and deceit that he now was? And, meanwhile , was every effort to change radically in the present or the near future doomed to failure”“And yet fear builds its phantoms which are more fearsome than reality itself, and reality, when calmly analysed and its consequences willingly accepted, loses much of its terror.”“We must remember that what our governments are doing today will set the tone for future administrations. The very powers that may be exercised, perhaps for adequate reasons today, may be exercised later for totally inadequate and perhaps even for objectionable reasons. It is always unsafe to weaken on principles.”“There is no end to the adventures that we can have if only we seek them with our eyes open.”“A moment comes, which comes but rarely in history, when we step out from the old to the new, when an age ends, and when the soul of a nation, long suppressed, finds utterance.”“A country under foreign domination seeks escape from the present in dreams of a vanished age, and finds consolation in visions of past greatness. That is a foolish and dangerous pastime in which many of us indulge. An equally questionable practice for us in India is to imagine that we are still spiritually great though we have come down in the world in other respects. Spiritual or any other greatness cannot be founded on lack of freedom and opportunity, or on starvation and misery.”“Loyal and efficient work in a great cause, even though it may not be immediately recognized, ultimately bears fruit”Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: US flight disruptions: Nationwide ground stop ordered for only the second time since 9/11
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The United States witnessed its second nationwide aviation disruption of this kind since the September 11, 2001, terror attacks after the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The United States witnessed its second nationwide aviation disruption of this kind since the September 11, 2001, terror attacks after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted departures across the country for more than four hours on Friday due to communications failures affecting multiple air traffic control centres. Although the FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET, widespread travel disruption continued, with more than 10,000 flights delayed or cancelled and airlines warning that cancellations could stretch into the weekend.The disruption, triggered by a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control facilities, forced airports to suspend departures and manage aircraft already on the ground. The FAA said it had ordered the halt as a precaution while technicians investigated the problem.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident posed a threat to the United States. Addressing reporters at the White House, he also ruled out an apparent cyberattack, saying the disruption “appears this was mechanically driven.”The FAA announced the lifting of the ground stop after air traffic control facilities began recovering. However, the resumption of departures did not immediately restore normal operations, as airlines and airports continued dealing with aircraft, crew and passenger disruptions.Also Read| US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US operationsAirlines prepare for further cancellationsAirlines began adjusting their schedules as the disruption continued, with carriers warning passengers of delays and cancellations. JetBlue Airways told staff it would cancel the remaining flights scheduled for Friday, except those operating on European routes, along with additional flights on Saturday. The move was aimed at ensuring aircraft and crew were positioned to resume normal operations, according to a memo seen by CNBC.A nationwide ground stop prevents aircraft from departing their airports of origin. Such disruptions can have a cascading impact on flight schedules, particularly when delays extend for several hours and flight crews approach their maximum permitted duty hours.According to aviation data firm Cirium, around 11,000 flights were scheduled to depart US airports after 4 p.m. ET on Friday. The disruption also resulted in approximately 600 diverted flights, including 104 that were redirected to other airports.International flights had begun departing from coastal hubs before 6 p.m. ET. The FAA said inbound international flights would be handled on a case-by-case basis.In an earlier statement on X, the FAA described the incident as a “temporary telecommunications outage” affecting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The agency said it had halted departures out of an “abundance of caution”.These centres are responsible for guiding aircraft at high altitudes along their routes. FAA technicians were investigating the communications failure, while the agency said flights would resume as en route traffic facilities recovered through coordination with the air traffic control system.Also Read| 'Extraordinary circumstances': US grounds all departing flights over safety concernsSecond nationwide disruption since 9/11Nationwide flight stoppages are extremely rare in the United States. Before Friday's disruption, the last nationwide ground stop was imposed in January 2023 following a technical failure in the Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system, which provides safety information to pilots.The only previous nationwide halt on a comparable scale came after the September 11, 2001, terror attacks, when authorities grounded aircraft across the country.Friday's incident comes amid repeated technical problems affecting US air traffic infrastructure in recent years.In September, hundreds of flights operating into Newark, New Jersey, and Philadelphia were cancelled, delayed or diverted after a Verizon fibre-optic cable was accidentally cut during construction work in New Jersey. The incident disrupted a backup data feed used by air traffic controllers.In 2025, air traffic controllers also lost contact with aircraft flying to and from Newark Liberty International Airport following an equipment failure. The incident triggered widespread flight delays and renewed concerns about ageing aviation infrastructure and staffing shortages.The precise cause of Friday's telecommunications outage was not immediately clear.Major US airlines issued statements saying they would assist passengers affected by the ground stop and urged travellers to check flight updates before heading to airports.You use AI every day. articles.title: UP man dies by suicide after strangling lover at Navi Mumbai lodge
articles.summary: NAVI MUMBAI: A 24-year-old man hailing from UP died by suicide after allegedly strangling a 23-year-old woman, with whom he was purportedly in a love
articles.body: NAVI MUMBAI: A 24-year-old man hailing from UP died by suicide after allegedly strangling a 23-year-old woman, with whom he was purportedly in a love relationship. The incident occurred at a lodge in Ulwe on the intervening night of Nov 11 and 12. Initially, the Ulwe police had registered an accidental death case.But, after the father of the deceased woman, residing in Ulwe, lodged a complaint at Ulwe police station alleging that his daughter was killed, a murder case was registered against the deceased accused.Subsequently, a final closure report (C-summary) will be submitted before the magistrate court, informed the police.Arjun Rajane, senior inspector of Ulwe Informed that the deceased accused was identified as Bharat Pankaj Bhardwaj, who had come from Gaziabad, UP and checked into room number 301 at Happy Residency Lodge in sector 9, Ulwe on Nov 11 at 6 pm. Thereafter, he called his lover to meet him at the lodge. The woman's murder and the accused's suicide came to light the next day early morning, when the hotel staff forcibly opened the door as Bhardwaj did not respond to door bells for room service.The woman was found strangled using nylon rope and Bhardwaj was found hanging to ceiling fan using another nylon rope. Both were rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital, where they were declared brought dead. An FIR of murder was registered against the deceased accused as per the complaint of the deceased woman's father and the opinion of doctor at Panvel sub-district hospital that confirmed the woman's cause of death was due to strangling.SPI Rajane said, "The motive of woman's murder and alleged suicide by Bhardwaj is not known as the woman's father has claimed that he was not aware whether his daughter was in a love relationship with Bhardwaj. Hence, Bhardwaj's parents have been summoned from UP for recording their statement. Also, the mobiles of both deceased have been seized for obtaining technical evidence of their conversation on WhatsApp chats and call data records to ascertain the motive of murder and suicide."Need help? articles.title: US flight disruptions: Ground stop lifted, but will your flight take off? Trump official explains
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted the nationwide ground stop that halted departures across the United States after a communications
articles.body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted the nationwide ground stop that halted departures across the United States after a communications failure disrupted air traffic control operations on Friday. However, passengers may still face delays and cancellations as airlines work to bring their aircraft and crew back into position.US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the problem had been identified and that air traffic control centres and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) facilities were operational again.The FAA reopened US airspace at 8.15 pm Eastern Time, allowing flights to resume.But Duffy cautioned that lifting the ground stop did not mean all flights would immediately take off. The recovery would depend on whether airlines had pilots and flight attendants available to operate their scheduled services."Does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It's going to be slow," Duffy said, advising passengers at airports to check directly with their airlines."We're going to try to move as many of those as we can tonight if we have the capacity with crews to move those flights. If not, we're going to start tomorrow morning with our airline partners, moving those aircraft. But it's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened this afternoon," he added.What caused the nationwide ground stop?Explaining the sequence of events, Duffy said instability in radar and communications systems was detected at 3.36 pm Eastern Time across air traffic control centres and TRACON facilities nationwide.The disruption led to inconsistencies in radar data and communications between controllers and aircraft. The FAA subsequently ordered a ground stop, following established safety procedures.Duffy said more than 3,500 aircraft were in the air when the order was issued. Most were able to land safely, and fewer than 400 remained in the airspace at the time of his latest update.He said the FAA had not lost all radar or TRACON capabilities, but the instability prompted officials to halt departures as a precaution. Certain essential operations, including medical evacuation flights, cargo services carrying critical medicines and law enforcement movements, were allowed to continue.Duffy attributed the failure to ageing air traffic control infrastructure, describing the system as "incredibly old" and saying that outdated hardware had gone down.The secretary also warned that similar disruptions could happen again unless the system was modernised. "You will have more of them unless the American people and the Congress tell us to build," he said, while acknowledging that he could not predict every possible failure.He referred to previous incidents in New York and Newark involving similar problems and urged lawmakers to approve funding for a complete overhaul.Trump administration seeks $50 billion for air traffic control upgradesThe Trump administration increased its request for air traffic control funding to $50 billion late Friday, after the communications failure forced the nationwide ground stop, Reuters reported.Earlier in the day, Duffy and the White House had sought $30.1 billion to upgrade the country's ageing airports and air traffic control infrastructure."This is an emergency," Duffy said. "What's more important than having an air traffic control system that actually works?"The $30.1 billion proposal included $10.1 billion for air traffic control modernisation, including a common automation platform, controller workstations and cloud computing. It also sought $2 billion to replace and improve FAA control towers and $18 billion for airport-related projects, including the modernisation or replacement of ageing terminals.The administration's request also comes after Congress approved $12.5 billion in July 2025 for air traffic control upgrades and increased recruitment of controllers. The FAA has said it has replaced 68% of its legacy copper telecommunications network with high-speed fibre infrastructure.Reuters reported that the Senate Commerce Committee said Friday's incident underlined the need to prioritise modernising the en route centres that manage traffic between airports. Congress has already approved $1.9 billion to replace outdated en route centres.The FAA's dependence on ageing technology has been a longstanding concern. The agency relies on decades-old computers and has sourced replacement parts through auction websites. Last week, it said it would replace floppy disks used for weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities by the end of 2028.Airlines warn of continuing delays and cancellationsEven after the FAA lifted the ground stop, airlines faced the task of repositioning aircraft and arranging available crews before they could resume normal schedules.Air Canada cancelled all flights to and from the US for the remainder of Friday evening because of the FAA order. The airline also warned that services between Canada, the Caribbean and South America that pass through US airspace could be affected.JetBlue cancelled the remainder of its domestic flights on Friday, with exceptions for certain Europe-bound services from Boston Logan International Airport and New York's John F Kennedy International Airport. The airline warned that disruptions, including further cancellations, could continue into Saturday, according to AP.The ground stop had affected thousands of flights. AP reported that at least 827 flights had been diverted by Friday evening, including 670 sent back to their original departure airports and 157 redirected elsewhere, according to aviation analytics company Cirium.Around 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to depart US airports after 4 pm Eastern Time, raising the prospect of further disruption.The stoppage also affected cargo operations and left several NBA, NHL and college sports teams stranded as they attempted to travel for weekend fixtures, AP reported.Passengers have been advised to check their flight status with airlines before heading to airports, as the resumption of departures does not guarantee that every scheduled service will operate.You use AI every day. articles.title: War through her eyes. She’s hero not victim
articles.summary: Women on Ukraine’s frontline writing (her)story The biggest dilemma posing war journals is how much of the self the author should allow to colour the
articles.body: Women on Ukraine’s frontline writing (her)storyThe biggest dilemma posing war journals is how much of the self the author should allow to colour the reporting of conflict. In Looking At Women Looking At War: A War and Justice Diary, author Victoria Amelina faces no such dilemma. She chronicles Russia’s war against Ukraine as one personally affected by it. And in the end, it is the war that would consume her – Amelina was killed in a Russian missile strike in the summer of 2023.This is why, Amelina speaks to us from her grave – the book was 60% finished at the time of her death. And rather than a simple accounting of war’s ravages, the book looks at women under siege, and their efforts at documenting injustice in extreme circumstances. Take, for example, the librarian of the small frontline village of Kapytolivka, occupied by Russians. Yulia Kakulya-Danylyuk is not just a librarian though, but her village’s recorder spirit. An entry in her war diary reads, “Today, I went to the library. I picked up some of my things; it’s a pity…I couldn’t take everything. It is painful to look at the books, everything is scattered, dirty, and smoky…The young boys almost begged me, saying they are not guilty and already want to go home. The strangest thing is that I wasn’t scared of them at all. I just wanted to tell them a lot!”In Kharkiv, Tetyana Pylypchuk is overseeing an important evacuation – of manuscripts, letters, and first editions of 20th century Ukrainian writers. They are precious cargo because they represent Ukraine’s soul and spirit. Tetyana won’t leave the books for a second – ready to die along with them, should a Russian missile hit.The book is replete with women who make extraordinary choices during war. They have agency. They help, they rescue, they organise, they defend, they fight back. Iryna Dovhan was captured and tortured in occupied Donetsk in 2014. She was released after a photo of her, scarred and beaten up, appeared in NYT. She moved to Kyiv, and didn’t run when the full-scale Russian invasion began in 2022. Instead, she would rush to the first major Russian attack site, to assist a medical unit.Zhenia Podobna in Irpin had witnessed the swarm of Russian attack helicopters moving towards Hostomel airport, north of Kyiv. Then she saw one being shot down, a pivotal moment, the first day of the full-scale war. So, Zhenia is determined to find the person who downed that first helicopter, and tell the world his or her story. Zhenia’s apartment would be shelled by Russians.Oleksandra Matviichuk wanted to be a theatre director, but chose to pursue justice instead, dedicating herself to documenting war crimes, going on to win the Peace Nobel in 2022 with her organisation. Casanova (a callsign) wants a peaceful house in the countryside. But she ends up evacuating people from the frontline, and giving a voice to the voiceless. These are women who refused to be victims, stepping up for people in their darkest hours. And they force us to look at women in the midst of war in a different light – not as poor victims, but heroes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on his 137th birth anniversary, which is also
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on his 137th birth anniversary, which is also observed as Children's Day across the country.In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Paying tribute to former PM Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary."Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid homage to the country's first prime minister, recalling his contribution to India's freedom struggle and his leadership during the early years of independent India.In a post on X, Rajnath said, "On the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Ji, I pay my tributes to him. His contribution to India’s freedom struggle and his leadership as the first Prime Minister of independent India left an enduring imprint on the formative years of our nation."Lok Sabha leader of opposition and former Congress chief Rahul Gandhi also paid tribute to Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary.In a post on X, Rahul described Nehru as the "jewel of India" and the country's first prime minister.He said freedom was not the destination but "a milestone in the nation's new journey", adding that Swaraj was not merely about power but about every citizen's participation and responsibility towards the country's future.Rahul also recalled Nehru's vision of India as an idea built on diversity, democracy and equality."Their dream of a modern, scientific, progressive, and self-confident India remains our inspiration today," he said, adding that efforts to build such an India would be the "true tribute" to Nehru.November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India to mark the birth anniversary of Nehru, who was popularly known as 'Chacha Nehru' because of his affection for children.After Nehru's death, it was unanimously decided to observe his birthday as 'Bal Diwas' or Children's Day in India. He was born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, and died on May 27, 1964.Nehru became India's first prime minister on August 15, 1947, after playing an active role in the country's freedom struggle.Schools across the country organise various activities for students on the occasion, including games and competitions. Government bodies also pay tribute to the former prime minister and hold commemorative events.The United Nations declared November 20 as Universal Children's Day in 1954. India initially observed Children's Day on the same date.However, following Nehru's death in 1964, Parliament unanimously passed a resolution to mark his birth anniversary on November 14 as National Children's Day.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A New Jersey theatre nearly faced demolition in the 1980s, but volunteers refused to abandon it; after a $130 million restoration, the 1929 landmark has reopened ahead of its first concert on November 13
articles.summary: The historic Loew’s Jersey Theatre has reopened after a $130 million restoration.
articles.body: The historic Loew’s Jersey Theatre has reopened after a $130 million restoration. The 1929 Wonder Theatre, which once faced demolition, is back under its marquee just in time for its first major show, the Trey Anastasio Band, on Friday, 13 November, ABC 7 reported.The reopening was marked by a grand ceremony attended by representatives from Jersey City, Hudson County and preservation groups involved in saving and restoring the historic theatre.A historic theatreOne of New Jersey’s most iconic historic venues, Loew’s Jersey Theatre first opened in 1929. It was one of five Loew’s ‘Wonder Theatres’ in the New York area. George Rapp designed it in a gilded Baroque-Rococo style. During the Great Depression and World War II, the theatre offered an escape that didn’t cost much. Speakers at the recent ribbon-cutting ceremony called it the ‘People’s Palace’, and the name has stuck.Back in the day, the theatre hosted some of the most famous performers of the era. The general manager, Bruce Wheeler, has repeated the legend that a 17-year-old Frank Sinatra bought a ticket in 1933 to see Bing Crosby and that it changed his life, NorthJersey.com reported. The building had that effect on people. Later, in the 1970s, the theatre became a cinema. Residents, including Hudson County Executive Craig Guy, still remember seeing The French Connection, Shaft and Jaws there.By the 1980s, the building had fallen on hard times and nearly faced demolition. What saved it was pressure from grassroots preservationists, led by the non-profit Friends of Loew’s. In the 1990s, the city bought the theatre and allowed the group to begin restoration work and run the building as a non-profit arts centre.However, the money never stretched far enough. A $1 million state grant, matched by the city, still left the project about $2 million short of meeting basic needs, including restoring the heating and getting the bathrooms working. Volunteers filled the gap through weekend work sessions. They repaired lighting and mechanical systems, mapped every seat, scraped away old paint and repainted the seats by hand. By 2001, they had done enough to partially reopen the theatre after 15 years without regular performances.The bill grew as the project dragged on. Former Mayor Steve Fulop estimated the cost at $40 million in 2020. The city announced a $72 million agreement the following year. By May 2025, delays and rising material costs had pushed the total to $130 million.OTJ Architects, working with Phelps Construction Group, restored the historic details while modernising the building. Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment, a partner in the project, helped bring the work across the finish line.‘The Loew’s really, for me, represents two things: The first is returning Journal Square as the heart of Jersey City. This should and can be the cultural capital of the city. We want Journal Square to really be a location where people go for arts, entertainment and food. This is going to be the return of the centrepiece of the renaissance of Journal Square,’ James Solomon, the mayor of Jersey City, said during Monday’s press event.The theatre is now back and kicking. It has new sound and lighting systems, and flexible seating for between 2,600 and 4,000 guests, depending on the event. Wheeler said that placing equipment in a historic room requires care. ‘You can’t put speakers in a place like this just anywhere. It has to be strategic,’ he told 6sqft.Not everything is finished. The grand lobby’s chandelier and the theatre’s organ are still undergoing repairs and will return in the coming months. But the important thing is that the theatre is now open. With Friday’s performance, the theatre will come back to life. The first community event will be the Mayor’s Holiday Concert on 2 December, which is free and open to the public. The calendar is already looking eventful, with The War on Drugs on Saturday, Jodeci on 18 November and comedy bookings through December and January.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Mick Jagger bought an 18th-century French chateau for about $477,000 in 1980; its 50-acre estate has a recording studio used by the Rolling Stones
articles.summary: Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger owns an 18th-century château in France’s Loire Valley, where he regularly spends time each summer and celebrates his
articles.body: Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger owns an 18th-century château in France’s Loire Valley, where he regularly spends time each summer and celebrates his birthday. The property, known as Château de Fourchette, is located in Pocé-sur-Cisse and was once the residence of Duke Étienne-François de Choiseul.Jagger’s connection to the region dates back to childhood holidays spent at a campsite nearby. He bought the rectangular building, topped by a mansard roof, in 1980 for 2.2 million francs, equivalent to about $477,000. According to Architectural Digest, the estate covers 50 acres and includes landscaped gardens, a professional recording studio and leisure facilities.Mick Jagger's French château has a history dating back to the 18th centuryThe château is in Pocé-sur-Cisse, a town in France’s Loire Valley, and is known as Château de Fourchette. Before Jagger owned it, the property was the residence of Duke Étienne-François de Choiseul, a celebrated army officer and diplomat who lived from 1719 to 1785.The singer was drawn to the area partly because he had spent his childhood holidays at the nearby Île d’Or campsite, about a 10-minute drive away. He bought the rectangular house, which has a mansard roof, in 1980 for 2.2 million francs, or $477,000. Jagger returns to the château every summer.The property is also associated with his annual birthday celebrations on July 26; locals say fireworks may sometimes be seen from the grounds.Mick Jagger’s Château de Fourchette features 50 acres of gardens and a swimming poolThe château is set within 50 acres of landscaped gardens, giving the historic property extensive grounds around the main building. The estate includes a pond, a waterfall, a swimming pool and a tennis court. It also has a Japanese pagoda, adding another distinctive feature to the grounds.The gardens are part of the setting where Jagger spends time during his summer visits. The singer takes on ordinary outdoor tasks, including tending his vegetable garden and pruning his rose bushes. He also looks after sheep and works on do-it-yourself projects around the property.These activities form part of the rural routine he enjoys at the French retreat, alongside cooking and playing guitar. The gardens are elegantly landscaped and surround the historic residence.Mick Jagger’s Château de Fourchette has a recording studio used by the Rolling StonesThe French château has a professional recording studio that has been used by the Rolling Stones. The band recorded its album ‘A Bigger Bang’ at the property. Released in 2005, it was the group’s first studio album following an eight-year break.During the COVID lockdown, the singer also filmed himself inside the château several times. One appearance was for ‘The Tonight Show’ with Jimmy Fallon. The property serves as more than a holiday home as it has also provided a place for the musician and his band to work. The recording studio remains one of the estate’s notable features.How bespoke furnishings shaped the interiors of Mick Jagger’s French châteauThe château’s interiors include furnishings made with fabrics selected for the residence. According to Architectural Digest, a retired upholsterer who worked on the residence's decor recalled using fine fabrics for its furnishings. He explained that the colours of the fabric appeared to change with the sunlight, making the room look different throughout the day. He also described the project as a rare opportunity to work with exceptionally beautiful materials and create armchairs using techniques he had not previously tried.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. articles.title: In 2016, a Dehradun engineer began building a portable ECG device after losing a friend to a heart attack; 10 years later, his startup says it has deployed 60,000 units across 20,000 villages
articles.summary: Rajat Jain was only 21 when he had to deal with one of the biggest traumas. He experienced a loss that changed the direction of his life.
articles.body: Rajat Jain was only 21 when he had to deal with one of the biggest traumas. He experienced a loss that changed the direction of his life. One of his closest friends died of a heart attack and he couldn’t do anything. But this gave him an inspiration to build something in the future that could save other young lives. Years later, his personal tragedy became an inspiration behind a portable ECG device designed to make cardiac screening accessible beyond hospitals.Meet Rajat, Dehradun inventor to build SpandanRanjan along with other co-founders created Spandan, a smartphone-connected ECG device that can record the heart's electrical activity and generate a report in about two minutes. What began as an attempt to address a deeply personal loss has grown into a healthcare technology initiative. It has a presence in some of the remotest regions of the country.As per a report published by The Better India, over 60,000 Spandan devices have been deployed across 28 states, reaching over 20,000 villages. The technology has reportedly been used to screen around five million patients, with the company attributing more than two lakh lives saved to its work.A personal tragedy which became an inspiration of inventionRajat was 21 and working in the automotive field after studying mechanical engineering. It was then he lost his friend to a heart attack. The incident made him look beyond his professional interests and towards a problem that affects millions of families. The early symptoms of the heart attack.The sad part is that heart attacks are unpredictable. It does not always announce itself with dramatic symptoms. Chest discomfort, breathlessness and other warning signs can sometimes be mistaken for gastric issues. In places where hospitals and specialists are far away, getting an ECG can involve travelling several kilometres, potentially delaying medical attention.How it all started, the team of 5In 2016, Rajat along with Arpit Jain, Saurabh Badola, Nitin Chandola and Sabit Rawat established Sunfox Technologies in Dehradun. The team started working on a device that could make ECG testing more portable and affordable and also accessible.In 2017, their first prototype was ready. The founders initially financed much of the work themselves. They faced skepticism about whether a medical device developed in India could match the reliability expected of conventional hospital equipment.How a smartphone became a portable ECG machineIt is a portable 12-lead ECG device that connects to a smartphone through cables and electrodes placed on the patient's body. The device captures the heart's electrical signals, while its accompanying software uses analytics and AI to generate an ECG report.An electrocardiogram (ECG) is among the first tests doctors recommend when a patient reports symptoms that could indicate a heart problem. It records the electrical signals produced by the heart and helps medical professionals identify abnormalities, including irregular rhythms and signs associated with a heart attack.Spandan was designed to make the process possible in smaller healthcare facilities.One of its important design features is that it draws power from the smartphone instead of requiring a separate battery. It can also work without an internet connection, making it useful in areas with unreliable electricity and network connectivity.According to Rajat, the device can be operated by healthcare workers with or without formal medical education, although clinical interpretation and medical decisions remain important parts of patient care. The company says its devices are available in different models, priced between Rs 6,900 and Rs 75,000.Fortis Hospital in UttarakhandIn 2018-19, Sunfox conducted a pilot at Fortis Hospital in Uttarakhand in collaboration with the SELCO Foundation. A subsequent study in 2021 at Fortis Escorts Hospital in Dehradun compared Spandan readings with those of a conventional ECG machine. Of the 153 patients enrolled, 110 were included in the final results. The readings matched in 108 of those 110 cases.Larger studies followed, including research involving 2,799 patients published in the Anatolian Journal of Cardiology in 2025. Rajat says the company has since conducted more than 30 studies and compared Spandan's performance with standard ECG machines in over 30,000 patients.Another important initiative came in July 2022, when the company partnered with the Uttarakhand government to organise a free cardiac screening camp at Sonprayag, the starting point of the Kedarnath trek.Pilgrims visiting the region could undergo ECG screening through trained local volunteers.During the first month, nearly 1,500 people were screened, and 59 were referred to a local doctor. The initiative demonstrated how portable technology could help bring basic cardiac screening closer to people travelling through remote mountain regions.Sunfox says it has deployed more than 60,000 Spandan devices across India, covering over 20,000 villages in 28 states. Its technology has reportedly been used to screen approximately five million patients.The company has also expanded its work with state governments. In Uttarakhand, it has been involved in screening pilgrims along the Char Dham Yatra route. According to Rajat, more than 13,100 pilgrims had been screened and 463 critical patients identified by October 2026.For Rajat, the journey from losing a friend at 21 to developing technology that can reach patients far from major hospitals represents more than the growth of a startup.While Spandan cannot replace a hospital, a cardiologist or emergency treatment, it can make ECG testing possible in smaller clinics and remote healthcare centres.You use AI every day. articles.title: Man books Rs 1.55 lakh Delhi-New York round trip, airline changes flight itinerary without his consent and travel website rejects refund despite zero-cancellation policy; consumer commission orders Rs 1.95 lakh payout
articles.summary: A consumer commission in Visakhapatnam has directed a travel booking website and an airline to pay Rs 1.95 lakh to a passenger after finding them guilty
articles.body: A consumer commission in Visakhapatnam has directed a travel booking website and an airline to pay Rs 1.95 lakh to a passenger after finding them guilty of changing his international flight itinerary without obtaining his consent, ultimately leaving him unable to undertake the planned trip. The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered the two companies to refund Rs 1.55 lakh to the passenger, pay Rs 30,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The complaint concerned a round-trip booking made by the passenger and his friend through the travel website. As per the original itinerary, they were scheduled to leave Delhi for New York on September 4, 2024, travel onwards to Miami and then Quito, before returning to Miami and New York. Their return journey to Delhi was scheduled for September 11, 2024.However, the passenger alleged that the flight timings were subsequently altered without his approval. He contacted the booking platform and told it that the revised schedule would not serve the purpose of his trip. He then sought cancellation of the tickets and a full refund, arguing that he had neither requested nor agreed to the changes. According to the complaint, the website continued sending him messages suggesting that the itinerary changes had been initiated at his request, despite the alterations being made by the airlines. His refund request was eventually rejected, although he had opted for a zero-cancellation policy.Defending itself, the travel website told the commission that the airline had made schedule changes after the tickets were confirmed. These changes were beyond its control and included the cancellation of the Miami-Quito flight. The website's counsel claimed that the passenger subsequently contacted the platform to explore alternative arrangements and that a revised itinerary was prepared at his request. When he later sought a refund, the airline refused it under its applicable policy.The counsel further argued that the zero-cancellation policy purchased by the passenger did not cover situations in which an airline rescheduled a flight from its originally scheduled time. The airline, meanwhile, argued that the changes had been communicated well before the scheduled journey and had not materially affected the passenger's travel plans. It alleged that the booking website had independently cancelled the original reservation and issued an entirely new itinerary.The airline also told the commission that it did not directly handle cancellations or refunds for bookings made through third-party agents. It said it had transferred Rs 14,545 to the travel website and that the responsibility for passing on the amount to the passenger rested with the platform. It further argued that the passenger and his friend had failed to check in for the first flight and were consequently marked as no-shows. According to the airline, standard international airline practice requires all subsequent sectors of an itinerary to be cancelled if a passenger does not board the first flight.The commission, however, found fault with the manner in which the original booking had been altered. It noted that the travel website had not responded to the passenger's specific allegation that his consent had never been obtained before changing the itinerary. The commission observed that the platform's silence on this issue indicated its acceptance of the allegation.The commission also took note of the website's admission that a new itinerary had been implemented despite the absence of the passenger's consent.It observed that the companies had unilaterally altered the travel plan without securing the passenger's approval. An intermediary acting prudently should not have initiated an alternative itinerary without obtaining written consent from the consumer, it said. Holding both the travel website and the airline liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, the commission directed them to refund Rs 1.55 lakh to the passenger, pay Rs 30,000 in compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: US flight chaos: What happens to planes already in air when FAA orders nationwide ground stop?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 following a communications failure across air
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 following a communications failure across air traffic control centres, thousands of passengers were already travelling aboard aircraft in the air. While departures were halted across the country, planes already airborne were allowed to continue flying and land safely under air traffic control supervision.The disruption raised an important question: What happens to an aircraft already thousands of feet above the ground when air traffic control systems experience a major failure?A ground stop does not automatically require aircraft in the air to make an emergency landing. Instead, aviation authorities manage airborne traffic based on available communication systems, radar coverage, weather conditions, airport capacity and the aircraft's position.During Friday's disruption, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that although the system experienced instability, authorities had not completely lost radar or communications and were able to land thousands of aircraft safely, Reuters reported.What happens to aircraft already airborne?A nationwide ground stop primarily restricts aircraft from taking off. According to the FAA's air traffic control procedures, a ground stop requires aircraft meeting specified criteria to remain on the ground. Such restrictions can be imposed when an air traffic control facility is unable or partially unable to provide services.The FAA also identifies preventing prolonged airborne holding and avoiding congestion in air traffic control sectors as reasons for imposing ground stops.Aircraft already in the air are handled separately. Air traffic controllers continue managing their movements using available systems and clearances. Depending on the situation, pilots may be allowed to continue towards their planned destinations, instructed to hold in designated areas or diverted to alternative airports.This approach was also followed during the January 2023 FAA system outage. In a document submitted to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the US government confirmed that aircraft already airborne when the nationwide ground stop was imposed continued flying to their destinations.However, as those aircraft landed, congestion increased at several airports. Some flights had to be diverted to prevent airport surface gridlocks before eventually being allowed to proceed to their intended destinations.IP/06What if pilots lose contact with air traffic controllers?A more complicated situation arises when an aircraft loses two-way radio communication with air traffic control.The FAA's Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM) lays down specific procedures for pilots facing such circumstances. The action depends on whether the aircraft is operating under visual flight rules (VFR) or instrument flight rules (IFR).Under VFR conditions: If two-way communication fails, pilots are expected to continue flying under visual flight rules and land as soon as practicable.Under IFR conditions: Pilots must follow the last route assigned by air traffic control. If they were receiving radar vectors, they must proceed according to the applicable instructions. They must also follow prescribed altitude and route procedures under federal aviation regulations.The FAA says pilots are expected to exercise their judgement during communication failures and can take emergency action when circumstances require it.How do pilots signal a communication failure?The FAA has a specific transponder procedure for aircraft that lose two-way radio communication.Pilots are instructed to set their transponder to Mode A/3, code 7600, to indicate a radio communication failure. This allows air traffic controllers to identify the aircraft's communication problem where radar coverage is available.Pilots are also expected to attempt to re-establish contact through previously assigned frequencies, emergency frequencies and other available communication channels.Why are diversions and holding patterns necessary?Even when aircraft can continue flying, a major air traffic control disruption can create problems at their intended destinations.If several flights arrive simultaneously or airport capacity becomes constrained, controllers may instruct aircraft to enter holding patterns, where they fly predetermined routes while waiting for clearance to land.If an airport cannot accommodate additional aircraft, pilots may be directed to alternate airports. This helps prevent congestion on runways, taxiways and parking areas.The November 13 disruption demonstrated how quickly such problems can spread. At least 827 flights had been diverted by 7:05 p.m. ET, according to Cirium data cited by CNN.What happens after the ground stop is lifted?Lifting a nationwide ground stop does not immediately restore normal flight operations.Airlines must reposition aircraft, arrange available pilots and cabin crew, and adjust schedules to accommodate delayed passengers. Aircraft diverted to other airports may also need to be moved back into their original operating schedules.Following Friday's disruption, the FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET. However, authorities warned that flight operations would resume gradually and that the recovery could take several days.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Philippine court orders arrest of jailed, US-wanted celebrity preacher
articles.summary: Palace denies timing of warrant is linked to Trump’s visit to Manila next week.
articles.body:
A Philippine court has ordered the arrest of jailed celebrity preacher Apollo Quiboloy , who is wanted in the US on child sex trafficking charges, in a step towards his possible extradition, according to the country’s Justice Department.

The department’s spokesman Polo Martinez told the AFP news agency on Saturday that the Makati Regional Trial Court issued the warrant of arrest and a hold-departure on Thursday after finding probable cause that he committed the offences charged.

The Philippine government filed its petition with a lower court on Monday, three months after Washington formally requested his extradition in August. Under Philippine law, the court must now hold hearings before deciding whether or not to hand him over.

The court issued the same orders against two co-accused, Teresita Dandan and Helen Panilag, both officers of Quiboloy’s Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) sect. The two women are still at large, according to local media reports.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, speaking on behalf of the Office of the President, denied that the warrant was timed to coincide with US President Donald Trump’s visit to Manila on November 17 for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit.

“No, it was probably just a coincidence,” she said, according to the Philippines News Agency.

Quiboloy, who calls himself the “appointed son of God”, is being held without bail while on trial for human trafficking in Pasig, which carries life in prison if convicted, AFP reported.

He also faces a child abuse trial in Quezon City, according to local media. He has denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty to the Philippine charges.

A US grand jury indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children and bulk cash smuggling, AFP reported.

The FBI identified Dandan as the “international administrator” of a fake charity operation, and Panilag as a former top church administrator in the US, according to local media reports.

Police said after his 2024 arrest that alleged victims were told they were having sex with the “spirit of God” and were threatened that “angels of death” would hunt them down if they told anyone, AFP reported.

The church said at the time that members had “freedom of choice”.

Quiboloy’s sect claims to have millions of followers and owns a television network.

He is a close ally of former President Rodrigo Duterte. He ran for Senate last year from prison and received 5.6 million votes, but lost, AFP reported.

articles.title: Garth Brooks: Ireland's love affair with the country music superstar
articles.summary: Country music superstar Garth Brooks will perform a multi-city tour of Ireland in 2027.
articles.body:
Fans of Garth Brooks will be brushing off their Stetsons and polishing their cowboy boots after the country music superstar announced he will be performing in multiple cities across Ireland in 2027.

The tour includes Belfast, Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork and will be the first time he has played in Northern Ireland since his King's Hall gig in November 1998.

The singer has said in the past that Ireland is his favourite place in the world to sing , and the love appears to be mutual as his first two Belfast concerts sold out, with an extra date already added.

So why has an American country music star remained so popular with Irish fans for so many years?

Cathy O'Reilly, who is originally from County Monaghan but lives in Belfast, managed to get her tickets for the very first show of Garth Brooks' tour on 21 May 2027 at Boucher Road Playing Fields.

She has already seen Brooks perform live before - twice during his run of concerts in Dublin in 2022 and her love of his music was passed on from her parents and uncles.

"It's growing up listening to him it brings me back to my childhood. My uncle gave me his cd, he didn't even buy me one - just gave me his because I loved him so much."

She believes the Irish link to the US and the fact that fans on the island give the best welcome to performers, are the reasons for Garth Brooks' popularity in Ireland.

"He [Garth Brooks] gives us energy and we're giving it back ten-fold nearly, and we're just so welcoming so he really enjoys coming here."

Peter Aiken, from Aiken Promotions, told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that the new Belfast gig is "red hot".

"There could be a fourth show in Belfast," he said.

Brooks is the biggest selling artist in US history and is the only artist to pass 200 million albums sold.

In 2014 about 400,000 fans booked tickets to five concerts he had planned for Dublin's Croke Park but Dublin City Council only granted permission for three of them.

Brooks said he would only perform all five concerts or none at all and so the shows were cancelled.

He returned to Dublin in September 2022.

Stephen Butler from Newtownabbey performs as a Garth Brooks' tribute act with the band Thunder Rolls.

His love for the musician also goes back to his childhood.

"My mother was a fan when I was younger, she was always playing his music and buying his albums so I loved the songs.

"I knew, with me loving Garth and there being such a following in Ireland, I knew it was the right thing to do."

He went to the Dublin concert in 2022 and while he hasn't yet got tickets for the Ireland dates next year, he hopes to get tickets to at least one of them closer to the time.

"I was able to get four or five tickets about a week or two before the Croke Park shows, I'll definitely go - I have to go.

"His band is amazing, he's amazing, and his songs - he's got an endless amount of anthems."

Butler said in order to embody the stage persona of Garth Brooks, you "have to be passionate about his music".

"I'm not saying I'm as good as Garth Brooks, but I definitely have his enthusiasm.

"I talk about him and how much I love him throughout the songs and I just identify with them as much as I can.

"My job is easy, I just have to go on there and get everybody singing along with me."

Butler says he thinks the reason Garth Brooks remains so enduringly popular in Ireland is because the people here identify so strongly with his songs.

"Everybody loves Friends In Low Places, people of Ireland love it, they love Callin' Baton Rouge.

"I speak to a lot of people after I play the shows and a lot of people identify with some of the words in the songs, they tell me about a relative that's passed and they seem to have some kind of identification with the songs Tomorrow Never Comes or Unanswered Prayers - it talks about love and about how Garth feels.

"And in amongst Thunder Rolls and the big hits that Garth has, he sings big rocky country rock and ballads, so it's exciting and it's sad - it's an emotional roller coaster," he said.

"And he's such a down-to-earth, genuine, caring person, he seems to be a good soul and I think people people identify with his personality.

"It's a big working-class country and they love someone that's genuine and that talks from the heart."

articles.title: Australian entrepreneur Briony Kennedy claims Adobe's $15,000-a-month upgrade cost Adorn Cosmetics millions, triggered a 30% sales drop and forced her to sell her family home; she is now suing Adobe
articles.summary: An Australian beauty entrepreneur is fighting to keep her business afloat after what she describes as a disastrous website upgrade involving software
articles.body: An Australian beauty entrepreneur is fighting to keep her business afloat after what she describes as a disastrous website upgrade involving software giant Adobe. Briony Kennedy, founder of Melbourne-based ethical beauty brand Adorn Cosmetics, claims a transition to Adobe's Commerce Platform turned into a financial nightmare, leaving her with millions of dollars in losses, mounting debt and a business on the brink of collapse.Kennedy, who founded Adorn Cosmetics in 2008, had built the brand into a successful make-up and skincare business that generated an annual turnover of $6 million at its peak. However, she claims that the company's fortunes took a dramatic turn after she decided to upgrade its website in 2021, moving from a basic platform to Adobe's Commerce Platform in the hope of expanding its digital reach and increasing sales.According to a report by the Daily Mail, Kennedy is now pursuing legal action against the US-based software company, alleging that the transition, which was expected to strengthen her online business, instead contributed to its financial downfall.Adorn Cosmetics founder says Adobe promised revenue growth of up to 94%Kennedy reportedly agreed to a contract costing her $15,000 per month after Adobe projected revenue growth of between 34 per cent and 94 per cent through the new platform.An Adobe press release issued at the time highlighted the platform's potential to help Adorn Cosmetics run more targeted marketing campaigns using its email database and social media following of nearly 100,000 people.Explaining why she decided to invest in the upgrade, Kennedy told the Daily Mail that data security was one of her primary concerns."I wanted to know that my data was secure," she said, adding that she later realised her existing website platform might have been sufficient for her business."Later down the track, I found out that the website I was already using would have sufficed," she added.Website launch delayed from three months to nine months, sales allegedly dropped 30%According to Kennedy, the transition was far more complicated than she had anticipated. What was initially expected to be a three-month project reportedly took nine months to complete. She also alleged that repeated delays and high staff turnover at Adobe made the process increasingly difficult for her team.Recalling the experience, she described the project as an "absolute s***show"."What was supposed to take three months took nine months to launch with nothing but tears from my staff," she said.Kennedy further claimed that her team was not provided with the promised credentials or adequate access to understand the technical problems affecting the website. She alleged that several essential features had not been configured properly when the platform was launched."There were so many things they had not set up. All it did was cause the demise of my business and 18 years of hard work," she told the publication.The entrepreneur also claimed that sales fell by 30 per cent after the new website eventually went live, adding to the financial pressure on the company.Founder claims she lost over $1 million in digital advertisingThe website problems were not the only financial setback Kennedy alleges she faced. She also claimed to have lost more than $1 million on advertising campaigns across Facebook and Instagram, which she said failed to direct customers back to the Adorn Cosmetics website.With the monthly platform costs continuing and expenses mounting, Kennedy said she found herself trapped in a contract while struggling to keep the business operational.The financial strain eventually forced her to make significant personal and professional sacrifices. According to the report, she reduced her workforce from 15 employees to just four and sold the family home to manage the mounting financial pressure.Although she did not disclose the exact amount of her losses, Kennedy told the Daily Mail that the figure ran into millions of dollars.Adorn Cosmetics moves to Shopify as founder pursues legal action against AdobeAfter struggling with the platform, Kennedy eventually abandoned Adobe and rebuilt the company's website using Shopify last year. However, by then, she said the business was already dealing with substantial debt and financial difficulties.Following unsuccessful mediation talks, the entrepreneur has now initiated legal action against Adobe, seeking to pursue her claims against the software company.Reflecting on the situation, Kennedy said she felt she had little left to lose."I've got nothing to lose as I've already lost everything," she said.The dispute highlights the potential financial risks small businesses can face when investing heavily in digital infrastructure without fully understanding the long-term costs and operational requirements.New customers give entrepreneur hope as she warns small businessesDespite the setbacks, Kennedy has not given up on Adorn Cosmetics. Support from existing customers and a recent surge in orders have offered her some encouragement as she attempts to keep the brand alive.She revealed that the business gained 100 new customers within just 48 hours earlier this week, giving her renewed hope amid the financial uncertainty.Kennedy has also decided to speak publicly about her experience to caution other small business owners against rushing into expensive technology upgrades without carefully assessing their requirements.Her advice is to understand the risks involved, examine the worst-case financial scenario and avoid replacing an existing system simply because a newer platform appears more attractive."Find out what the worst-case scenario is. If things are working, don't chase the new shiny thing," she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
