articles.title: Russian casualties ‘reach 450,000’: What that means for the Ukraine war
articles.summary: Leaked Russian records reveal a war toll that falls hardest on older men, poorer regions and foreign recruits.
articles.body:
Records leaked from Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, have shown that at least 450,000 Russians, most of them soldiers, died in the war in Ukraine up to August this year.

Among the dead were more than 4,000 foreign citizens who are believed to have died fighting for Russia, from countries including Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Nepal, Colombia and Nigeria.

The records were obtained by two hacking groups, the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Ukraine’s Silent Crow.

Rosstat confirmed it had been hit by cyberattacks between October 29 and November 1, but said it found no evidence that its databases had been compromised or that protected data leaked.

Moscow does not officially publish its military death toll.

Deaths can take months, and sometimes years, to be registered, in Russia. Investigations for The Financial Times (FT) have concluded that once late paperwork is counted, the toll up to August will settle at about 550,000.

So what do the leaked records show, and what do they tell us about who is fighting Russia’s war? Here’s what you need to know:

The Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow said on November 1 that they had broken into Rosstat’s network.

The two hacking groups published their own analysis of the records and shared the files with several news organisations, though the data has not been independently verified.

However, media outlets and analysts say they believe it is real.

Janis Kluge, an expert on Russia at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, wrote on X: “There is no longer any doubt that the leaked Rosstat database is authentic. You can find any famous person who has died in recent years.”

However, in a later post he added: “The trickier question is: Was the data manipulated to increase the war death toll?” before adding, “This would [be] unbelievably difficult, so this is a highly unlikely conspiracy theory”.

A death toll far beyond anything Moscow has admitted so far.

The files list about 410,000 deaths directly as war-related, and 42,000 more fighting-age men whose deaths were confirmed in court because their bodies have never been recovered.

The FT identified another 12,000 likely military deaths among men who died at or near the front, bringing the total to at least 450,000.

Where have most of those Russian casualties occurred?

About 120,000 of those with a recorded location died in the area containing Avdiivka and Pokrovsk, and a further 48,000 in Bakhmut, the FT reported.

Avdiivka is a small industrial city in the Donetsk region. After Russian-backed forces seized parts of eastern Ukraine in 2014 and 2015, it became part of the so-called “contact line”, and Ukrainian forces spent years fortifying the city.

When Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, it was the subject of two years of bitter fighting before Russia took it in 2024.

After the fall of Avdiivka, Russian forces moved towards the coal-mining city of Pokrovsk in the Donetsk region, capturing it in early 2026 after more than a year of gruelling battles that had left the city in ruins.

Bakhmut, a city in the Donetsk Oblast and situated at a vital intersection connecting eastern Ukraine with the rest of the country, was the site of the longest and bloodiest infantry battle of the war before falling to Russian and paramilitary Wagner Group forces in May 2023.

Older men from poorer, often minority regions.

The average age of those killed rose from 34 in the first year of the war to 40 in 2025, and men aged 35 to 44 made up the largest group, with 158,000 dead, the FT reported.

Ethnic Russians constitute more than two-thirds of Russia’s population of 143 million. The rest are minorities – from millions of ethnic Ukrainians and Tatars to smaller Indigenous groups in Siberia and the Arctic.

Zabaykalsky Krai, home to a large community of Buryats, an Indigenous Mongolic people of southern Siberia, recorded about 12,300 deaths, roughly one for every 80 people in the region, the FT reported.

Bashkortostan, another region with a large minority population including Indigenous Bashkirs and Volga Tatars, recorded 15,800 deaths.

How many foreign fighters have been killed?

The FT identified 4,141 probable foreign soldiers holding foreign citizenship among the dead.

Bloomberg News, using a wider definition that includes people born outside Russia, counted 11,335, with foreign deaths rising from about 630 in 2022 to more than 5,500 in 2025.

Deaths of Nepalis were concentrated in 2023 and 2024, and those of Colombians, Kenyans and Nigerians from late 2025, Bloomberg reported.

The FT counted the highest death toll from Uzbekistan at 807, followed by Tajikistan with 598. There were also 44 Nepali dead and 98 Colombians, the highest toll from Latin America.

About 340 Africans are among the dead, most of them killed since 2025, Bloomberg reported.

Nigeria, Cameroon and Egypt had the highest tolls, with 127 deaths between them, according to the FT.

Furthermore, Ukrainian officials believe Russia deployed some 14,000 North Korean troops to hold off Ukraine’s 2024 incursion into the Kursk region, but they do not appear in the leaked data.

Mostly for the money, and often after being misled.

An estimated 28,000 foreigners from 136 countries are said to be fighting in the Russian army overall.

An Amnesty International report in September found that people from Brazil, Colombia, Sri Lanka and South Africa had been promised well-paid civilian jobs and then forced into the army on arrival in Russia.

The rights group spoke with foreign nationals currently serving with Russian forces and members of their families as well as lawyers, human rights activists and journalists.

It found local agents and misleading online job advertisements were being used to deceive foreign nationals in their home countries.

Nationals from 36 African countries are known to be fighting for Russia in the four-year war, Ukraine’s foreign minister said in November last year.

One South African man who applied online for a driving job in Poland was told to fly to Moscow, pick up a truck, and drive it to Poland.

His wife told Amnesty International: “Upon arrival to Moscow, everything was taken from him. He was told that he would not be going to Poland and that he is becoming a soldier.”

Many recruits were promised lucrative salaries and sign-up bonuses that were not then fulfilled, Amnesty reported.

In Kenya , where intelligence officials say more than 1,000 citizens have been recruited, agencies promised monthly wages of about $2,715 and bonuses of up to $9,309.

Moscow denies coercing anyone to fight in Ukraine.

What do these casualty figures mean for the war in Ukraine?

They indicate that Russia is struggling for manpower.

The Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, posted an analysis of the leaked data, saying the figures likely understate Russia’s true losses because of reporting limitations.

It added that, as of July, Russia’s casualties are now outpacing its recruitment.

Kluge told The Moscow Times that the deaths also represent about half a per cent of Russia’s working-age population, which may have little economic impact, so the main significance is political.

He added, “You cannot say Russia is winning this war if it is losing population at this rate.”

articles.title: Media can’t muster any outrage or coverage of violent comments from the left
articles.summary: Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan laughed about the Charlie Kirk assassination on their podcast, sparking outrage across conservative media.
articles.body: In spite of all the thrills traveling up the legs of the broadcast news veterans over the "blue tsunami" of the midterms, not everyone on the left is celebrating the victories with class and civility. But when leftists engage in the nastiest speech, they know that their liberal friends will carefully edit that out. The elitist networks will pretend that kindness, compassion and decency are hallmarks of their progressive movement. That’s why the nastiest speech must be hidden. None of the broadcast networks touched any of this. The conservative media exploded in outrage over podcaster Jennifer Welch and her sidekick Angie "Pumps" Sullivan when they laughed uproariously over a joke about the Charlie Kirk assassination. Welch and Sullivan starred in a Bravo reality series called "Sweet Home Oklahoma." Their podcast is called "I’ve Had It," and conservatives have definitely had it with their ugly speech. But their YouTube channel has over 1.8 million subscribers. WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN On Nov. 5, they were reading comments from their fans in an episode titled "Drinking MAGA Tears." Welch announced: "Dead Moroz says, ‘we’re digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again.’" They bowed their heads in laughter for 10 seconds. Sullivan felt it necessary to add, "Other than he was shot by somebody that was super-MAGA," and Welch echoed, "He was shot by a MAGA person." Late night host Jimmy Kimmel’s lie keeps getting repeated. Collin Rugg’s clip of this bilge on X has more than 7 million views and more than 19,000 likes. CHARLAMAGNE THA GOD CALLS OUT DAVE CHAPPELLE'S KIRK COMMENTS, WOULDN'T WISH THEM 'ON MY WORST ENEMY' Welch is a popular figure, not only on her podcast, but on other liberal podcasts, where hosts think her nastiness is a balm. On Instagram, former CNN anchor Don Lemon touted her appearance on his show with the question: "In need of a political detox?" In Lemon’s head, it’s a purging of toxins to be toxic. Two days after the Welch giggles, comedian Dave Chappelle seconded that nasty emotion on the stage of his "Karmageddon" tour stop at Madison Square Garden: "It’s scary being a public speaker. Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly but … I feel better." There were laughs and scattered applause. "I know I shouldn’t say that, but it’s just a feeling," he added. "I just be driving around, like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood … oh!" A YEAR AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER, SOME COMICS ARE CALLING OUT JOKES ABOUT HIS DEATH Then Chappelle concluded with the vision of Kirk in hell: "I’m sure Charlie Kirk is looking up at us right now, laughing so hard he can’t breathe." Comedian Tony Hinchcliffe delivered a nearly identical punchline about George Floyd in May at a roast for Kevin Hart. Back in April, National Public Radio celebrated Chappelle in a long "Newsmakers" interview for YouTube – in large part because he donated a cool $5 million to the NPR station in Dayton, Ohio. Chappelle boasted about comedians: "We're like a nation's kidney. We help everyone metabolize not just facts but feelings around facts or ideas." Is that what the dead Charlie Kirk jokes do? Purify the body politic? TURNING POINT USA SPOX ANDREW KOLVET SPEAKS OUT AS JENNIFER WELCH, DAVE CHAPPELLE MOCK CHARLIE KIRK'S MURDER Charlie’s widow Erika Kirk responded bluntly on X: "To see leftist podcasters, comedians, and commentators laugh about political assassination as though it’s entertainment and the destruction of a human life is a punchline, is beyond disgusting. … A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay." But most people didn’t see the leftists laugh. The same broadcast networks that routinely treat the president’s Truth Social posts as overwrought and uncivil couldn’t locate these clips. It's not "newsworthy" when the left is vicious. CHAPPELLE, JENNIFER WELCH JOKES ABOUT KIRK'S MURDER PART OF PATTERN OF LEFTISTS FINDING HUMOR IN VIOLENCE So, there’s assassination commentary, and then there’s execution commentary. Scott Galloway, a prominent multi-millionaire New York University professor and podcaster, acidly expressed that Elon Musk should be executed as a "traitor to the West." Why? Because his company Space X restricted Starlink satellite internet speeds in Ukraine last month. Musk said using Starlink "for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed." The elitist networks will pretend that kindness, compassion and decency are hallmarks of their progressive movement. That’s why the nastiest speech must be hidden. None of the broadcast networks touched any of this. Galloway argued this led to Ukrainian civilian deaths and proclaimed on his "Prof G" podcast: "And my question is, or my thesis is, we took the Rosenbergs and put them up against a wall and executed them for being traitors. And I realize this is an incendiary statement, but I’ll make it, and I believe it." CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION On a recent episode of the "Pivot" podcast with co-host Kara Swisher, Galloway repeated it: "We lined up the Rosenbergs against a wall. This is a traitor to the West, and he should be held to the same standards as every other traitor in the West." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Shortly after this, Galloway claimed that he hated Musk so much that he sold his Tesla, but not before defecating in the passenger seat. These unhinged haters are the people that media elites would like you to consider the enlightened voices of a brighter future. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM TIM GRAHAM

articles.title: The new center of gravity in Europe
articles.summary: Central and Northern European states are becoming Europe’s economic backbone and increasingly its military one.
articles.body:
Last week, Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that Poland had thwarted a Russian provocation along its border with Moscow’s Kaliningrad exclave. The episode underscores a larger reality: The frontline of European security runs through Central Europe, and the continent’s center of gravity has shifted.

Central and Northern European states are becoming Europe’s economic backbone and increasingly its military one. They occupy a strategic space that is both a focal point of Russian pressure and a target of Chinese influence.

As Western Europe’s traditional centers of political and economic power contend with domestic pressures and political instability, Central and Northern European nations are assuming a greater role in the continent’s growth, industrial renewal and defense.

The region is home to some of the European Union’s fastest-growing economies. In 2025, Poland’s GDP grew by 3.6 percent , Lithuania’s by 2.9 percent and the Czech Republic’s by 2.6 percent .

Germany’s industrial engine, weakened by high energy costs and Chinese competition, remains Europe’s largest and most important economy and manufacturing base. But its established industrial hubs are increasingly complemented by capacity across the Czech Republic, Estonia, Lithuania, Poland and Slovakia. These countries have recently outperformed in new industrial enterprise births per capita. Europe’s industrial strength is expanding eastward.

The region is also an emerging innovation hub. Affordable operating costs, highly skilled talent and strong research institutions have fueled entrepreneurial ecosystems in Prague, Riga, Tallinn and Warsaw.

Better integration of these industrial and technological strengths could create more secure European supply chains — and significant opportunities for the United States. A thriving integrated tech-industrial corridor in Central Europe will attract American investment, create partnerships for U.S. firms and strengthen the transatlantic economic motor.

Realizing this potential will require secure, affordable energy. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Europe has learned the costs of dependence on Russian hydrocarbons. Diversifying energy supplies and expanding interconnectors, pipelines and storage capacity will give Europe the means to eventually eliminate its remaining dependence on Russian energy.

But Europe must avoid replacing one strategic vulnerability with another. China’s dominance of green technology supply chains presents a significant challenge. The United States can help address it. Beyond liquified natural gas exports, American companies can partner with European counterparts on civil nuclear technology, including small modular reactors, electricity grid modernization and efforts to diversify green technology supply chains away from China.

Militarily, Central Europe is becoming an essential pillar of NATO. Poland fields the alliance’s third-largest military, behind only the United States and Turkey. The region also leads in defense investment . Lithuania, Estonia and Poland, which invest 5.33 percent, 5.10 percentand 4.68 percent of GDP, respectively, are approaching or already exceeding the alliance’s ambitious defense spending benchmark adopted at NATO’s Hague Summit.

Germany’s transformation is equally consequential. On track to spend $147 billion on defense in 2026, Germany’s defense budget this year will exceed the combined 2022 defense budgets of France, Germany and Italy.

Berlin has set an ambitious goal of developing the Bundeswehr into Europe’s strongest conventional military. In April, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius outlined plans to expand Germany’s military to 460,000 by 2039. If realized, German and Polish military expansion would create a formidable conventional defense core at the heart of NATO.

But military strength depends on more than spending and troop numbers. As Palantir Chief Technical Officer Shyam Sankar observed at a public forum last month: “Your deterrence was never your stockpile… It was your ability to generate the stockpile.” Central Europe’s industrial capacity and ability to scale production will be critical to deterring and, if necessary, defending against Russian aggression.

Beyond the renewal of military capabilities, Central and Northern European infrastructure is also critical to collective defense. The region provides strategic depth and is home to key depots, logistical corridors and staging areas that could prove decisive in a future conflict with Russia. The geography of Europe dictates that infrastructure in places like the Czech Republic, Germany and Poland will factor significantly into any future war.

No discussion of Europe’s security architecture is complete without Ukraine. Its sovereignty, territorial integrity and successful integration into European economic and security structures are essential to a secure transatlantic future. Ukraine’s defeat, by contrast, would profoundly undermine it.

The arteries already connecting Ukraine to the region have enormous potential to mature and expand. Growing ties to Ukraine, particularly its defense industrial capacity, can further energize the core of European economic and military power.

Faced with acute challenges posed by an authoritarian axis and increasingly constrained resources, the United States must recognize that its future security depends in large part on factoring the strength and production capacities of its allies into its strategic calculations.

Nowhere is this more important than in Central Europe. Its geography, population, technological innovation, industrial base and expanding military capabilities make it an indispensable pillar of American engagement in Europe.

Our adversaries recognize the region’s importance as well. The region is a prime target of persistent Russian grey-zone attacks and information warfare, while Beijing has worked assiduously to weaken its ties with the United States.

The heart of Europe is emerging as a chief architect of the continent’s future; Washington should treat it accordingly.

Daniel Kochis is a senior fellow in the Center on Europe and Eurasia at Hudson Institute .

articles.title: Sagittarius, Weekly Horoscope, November 15 to November 21, 2026: Push through work pressure and welcome family support while prioritising health and financial discipline
articles.summary: General: The week opens with fire in your feet and too many thoughts in your head.
articles.body: General:The week opens with fire in your feet and too many thoughts in your head. Early on, you'll feel brave enough to attempt something unusual, the kind of task others avoid or postpone. Short trips, errands across town, a quick visit to a relative, or even repeated commuting for practical reasons may keep you on the move. Yet your body may not fully agree with your enthusiasm. Energy rises and dips strangely, so don't act as if you're made of steel. If you've been thinking of making a big practical purchase, especially something related to travel or transport, wait a bit. Not every urge needs instant action.By the middle of the week, the pressure builds. Work piles up, messages keep coming, and patience feels thinner than usual. Still, this is also the part of the week where your inner resolve gets stronger. Someone younger, perhaps a sibling or a cousin with fresh perspective, can give useful support. A major decision may take shape in your mind, and once you make it, you'll work with real grit. Thursday has a slightly crowded feeling, like a market street before sunset. There could be neighbourly interaction, a social call, or a cheerful event close to home. An old friend may reappear, bringing memories and a needed change of mood.By Friday and the weekend, the air softens. Home feels kinder. You begin to put down the bundle of small tensions you've been carrying all week. Family company, a gathering, or time spent laughing over food and familiar stories will do you good. The weekend has the smell of rain after dust, relief at last. There may also be a practical family gain, support from parents, or a useful household decision. Save what you can. This is not the week to scatter your resources in ten directions.Love and Relationships:Partnership matters begin on a touchy note. At the start of the week, one sharp exchange with your spouse or partner can grow bigger than it deserves if both of you insist on having the last word. The real issue may not be the topic itself but fatigue, ego, and poor timing. Choose your moment. A serious conversation in the middle of a rushed morning won't help anyone. If you're single, you may also feel impatient with mixed signals. Don't push for clarity on a day when everyone is already stretched.As the week moves ahead, the strain begins to ease. Tuesday and Wednesday are better for practical understanding than dramatic emotion. Your partner may not be especially expressive, but steadiness counts too. Routine can become healing now. Share ordinary life, a meal at home, a quiet cup of tea, planning children's studies, or discussing family expenses without turning it into a battlefield. Children, if you have them, bring brighter news this week and give you both something hopeful to focus on. Their efforts, results, or happy progress can lighten the home atmosphere.Thursday and Friday bring warmer social energy. New friendships, better terms with neighbours, and support from your spouse create a more pleasant rhythm. If you've been carrying resentment, this is the time to put it down gently. By the weekend, affection becomes easier to show. Family functions, visiting relatives, or simply sitting together without rushing anywhere can repair more than a long speech would. Your bond with your mother or a motherly figure looks especially smooth. Love doesn't always arrive with thunder. Sometimes it returns like evening breeze through an open window.Education and Career:This week asks for courage first, comfort later. Early in the week, you may take on a task that looks bigger than your current energy level. Good. You're capable of more than you think, but you must respect the process. Don't expect applause on day one. Tuesday and Wednesday are all about effort, revision, persistence, and mental toughness. If you're employed, your desk may fill up faster than you clear it. If you're in business, progress comes from follow-up, calls, movement, and not leaving loose ends for tomorrow. Honest work pays. Shortcuts won't.Students have a mixed but mostly hopeful week. Midweek supports concentration on core goals, especially if you've already been disciplined. Results can come through consistency, not panic. If you have exams, project deadlines, or coaching classes, keep the schedule plain and practical. Read. Revise. Repeat. Midweek can bring the satisfying feeling that your hard work is beginning to show. Yet Friday may scatter attention a little, especially if the home atmosphere turns cheerful and distracting. Don't let one lazy evening become a lost study block.For professionals, the best gains come after the heaviest effort. Thursday may feel crowded with demands, but it can also bring useful contacts. A neighbour, old friend, or casual acquaintance could say something that sparks an idea or opens a path. Keep your ears open. By Friday, domestic harmony helps you work better because your mind is less pulled by emotional noise. The weekend isn't only for rest. It's also good for reviewing plans, clearing pending messages, and deciding where your energy should go next. One bold decision this week can shape the month ahead.Money and Finance:Money matters stay steady but not flashy in the first half of the week. You can earn, but mostly through effort, overtime, extra calls, extra trips, or simply not giving up when the work feels dull. Early on, keep your spending measured. This is not the ideal time to buy a vehicle, no matter how tempting the offer looks or how convinced a salesperson sounds. Delay is your friend here. Average cash flow is manageable if you don't create unnecessary pressure with impulsive purchases.The middle of the week teaches a plain lesson. Money comes from sweat, not luck. You'll do best with practical budgeting, timely bill payments, and fewer mood-based expenses. Avoid too much outside eating as well, not only for health but because these little spends add up when the week is already busy. Thursday may bring social expenses, a contribution to a local celebration, travel cost, or small hospitality spending. Fine, but keep your hand light. Don't open your wallet every time emotion stirs.The tone improves beautifully toward Friday and the weekend. There are signs of hidden or unexpected support, money from a side source, family help, an old due payment, or gain through property matters. If you're considering a house, plot, or home-related investment, the later part of the week looks much kinder than the beginning. A profitable deal is possible if you read the details and don't rush from excitement. Weekend energy also supports savings. Put something aside before spending on comforts. Money kept safely now will comfort you later.Health and Well-being:Your health needs respect this week, especially because your spirit may run faster than your body. At the start, courage is high but physical sensitivity is also present. Don't ignore signs like low energy, acidity, disturbed sleep, or body strain from rushing about. Travel, even short distance travel, can tire you more than usual. Drive carefully and avoid acting in haste on the road. If you've been skipping meals, surviving on tea, or eating at odd hours, your system will complain. Listen before it shouts.Midweek can bring restlessness. Not exactly illness, but that agitated feeling where the mind keeps spinning and the shoulders stay tight. Heavy workload is the main reason. Break your tasks into chunks. Step away from your phone now and then. Eat simple food. Thursday especially asks you to avoid outside food or anything too oily and careless. An old friend's visit or a happy local event may lift your mood, and that emotional easing will help the body too. Sometimes half the headache is worry.The better news comes later. Friday begins a gentle release, and by the weekend your nervous system gets room to breathe. Family time, laughter, familiar cooking, and support from your mother or maternal side can be unexpectedly healing. If you've been carrying too much tension in silence, this is a good weekend to rest without guilt. Sleep properly. Stretch a little. Sit in the sun for a while. Your health improves not through grand plans this week, but through simple care repeated faithfully.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates.
